tasks.short: Encourage and accompany patients in work, social and recreational activities, plan each patient's activity schedule, and note participation.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician plans each patient's weekly activity schedule on paper
Psychiatric technician encourages patients to develop work skills and participate in social and recreational activities

tasks.design: Each patient's weekly activity schedule is built in the record ({OTHER}) from the activities in their treatment plan and the ward's activity calendar, instead of on paper. Participation is ticked on a tablet list per activity. Encouraging and accompanying patients stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules were written by hand and participation noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Care records can hold activity calendars and tick lists.
tasks.still_hard: Patients' moods change plans every day.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a withdrawn patient to join the kitchen group.

reach.learn: Whether participation is visible per patient.

evidence.claim: Care records can hold activity calendars and participation tick lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to participation noted; therapy itself is outside.
Input contract: activities in the treatment plan; fallback is paper schedules.
research_questions: Does participation rise when schedules are visible?

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician keeps the ward activity calendar current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small ward; high: many patients with individual schedules.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe patients' physical and emotional well-being, note observations in the record, and report unusual behavior or ailments to medical staff.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician monitors patients' physical and emotional well-being
Psychiatric technician writes observations in the record
Psychiatric technician reports unusual behavior or physical ailments to medical staff

tasks.design: Observations go into structured fields on a tablet in the record ({OTHER}) during the shift, and non-urgent findings are flagged for the physician's next round in the record instead of a phone call. Urgent findings are still reported in person or by phone. Observing patients stays with the technician; no camera or software analyses patients' behavior.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were typed at the end of the shift and every finding was phoned through.
tasks.enabler_now: Care records take structured observations on tablets and flag items for rounds.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle changes in mood are hard to put in fields.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a patient is more agitated than usual.

reach.learn: Whether observations are available at rounds.

evidence.claim: Care records can take structured observations and flag items for physician rounds.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ward shift to staff informed; medical treatment is outside.
Input contract: tablets on the ward; fallback is typing at shift end.
Urgent findings are still reported at once.
Medical staff check flags at rounds as they took calls.
research_questions: Are non-urgent findings seen at the next round?

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician checks that flags were seen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few non-urgent findings; high: a ward with many observations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take temperature, blood pressure and other measures of physical condition, and record the values in the patient record.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician takes measures of patients' physical condition with thermometers and blood pressure gauges
Psychiatric technician records the values on paper and types them into the record

tasks.design: Connected thermometers and blood pressure monitors send values to the record ({OTHER}) after a wristband scan, so values are not written on paper and typed later; the technician checks the values on screen. Taking the measurements stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were written on paper and typed in at the end of the round.
tasks.enabler_now: Connected measurement devices send values to records by wristband scan.
tasks.still_hard: Some patients refuse devices or wristbands.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a patient who fears the blood pressure cuff.

reach.learn: Whether values are in the record sooner.

evidence.claim: Connected measurement devices can send values to patient records by wristband scan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the measurement round to values recorded; acting on values is outside.
Input contract: devices connected to the record; fallback is paper.

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician enters values by hand when a patient refuses the wristband.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few measurements; high: daily rounds for many patients.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and influence patients' behavior by talking with, teaching, counselling and befriending them, and note significant interactions.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician observes and influences patients' behavior by communicating, teaching and befriending them
Psychiatric technician notes significant interactions in the record

tasks.design: Significant interactions are noted on a tablet in short structured fields in the record ({OTHER}) during the shift instead of free text at the end. Talking with, teaching and befriending patients stay with the technician; conversations are not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed in free text at the end of the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Care records take short structured notes on tablets.
tasks.still_hard: Much of the work is presence, which does not fit a field.
tasks.human_edge: Being the person a frightened patient trusts.

reach.learn: Whether notes are complete at team meetings.

evidence.claim: Care records can take short structured notes on tablets.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ward shift to interactions noted; therapy is outside.
Input contract: tablets on the ward; fallback is typing at shift end.
Interacting with patients does not change.

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician learns the note fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few notes; high: a busy ward with many notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The psychiatric technician keeps encouraging, observing, measuring and befriending patients; paper schedules, retyped values and end-of-shift typing shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the record on a tablet
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time with patients.
